ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and SOR/2002-184; FINTRAC Guidance for reporting entities; Quebec Act respecting the transparency of enterprises, CQLR c. T-11.1 (register of ultimate beneficiaries, sections 3-19, creating a non-public government-access register); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1 (QBCA); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44 (CBCA), as amended by Bill C-42 beneficial-ownership transparency provisions; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46 (money laundering and terrorist financing offences).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the Quebec register of ultimate beneficiaries (Registre des beneficiaires ultimes) is accessible to the Registraire des entreprises, Revenu Quebec, police authorities, intelligence agencies and financial supervisors; it is not publicly searchable. Corporate registers under the CBCA are similarly restricted pending full implementation of the federal registry access regime.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory onboarding and ongoing screening against FINTRAC risk-based compliance standards; mandatory checks against the Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list (Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act), UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (given USD settlement rails), and UK HMT consolidated list; enhanced due diligence mandatory for PEPs, Heads of International Organizations, family members and close associates under PCMLTFA SOR/2002-184, with source-of-wealth verification; industry risk tier is Low_Risk_Standard, but payment processors Stripe and Wise, as reporting entities, will conduct independent KYC/AML and may impose enhanced verification on non-resident UBOs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — Clé d'accès online filing portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); NUANS name search report; federally, Corporations Canada online filing centre if CBCA incorporation is selected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), every enterprise name must be in French or registered with an identical French-language form; the name in the REQ register must use Latin script with standard accented characters; a foreign-language name is permissible only when accompanied by an approved French version (e.g., 'IA Studio PostProduction' with French form 'Studio de postproduction IA'); logos, signage and the register's operative name must comply with statutory French-language requirements.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de commerce / Chamber of Commerce
Conseil / Advisory or Council (where implying professional regulatory status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The 90-day reservation window is non-renewable; upon expiry, a new NUANS report and reservation application must be filed with a fresh fee. On rejection, the applicant may (i) file a corrected name reservation request with a revised name; (ii) for sensitive tokens, obtain prior ministerial or regulatory authorization and re-file; and (iii) appeal the Registraire's decision to the Court of Quebec (administrative and municipal division) within 60 days of notification under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), supported by written submissions and the NUANS report.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable on a qualified basis: Quebec law requires a real, physical head office (siege social) in Quebec for service of process and for access to corporate records; a virtual-office service providing a physical Quebec street address, mail handling and registered-agent functions is market-standard and meets registry compliance, but Revenu Quebec and the Canada Revenue Agency will scrutinize management-and-control situs for corporate residence and GST/QST registration; third-country management combined with a pure virtual address materially increases the risk of deemed non-resident status or agency exposure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 10-15% annualized probability of a soft verification or unannounced physical on-site inspection by Revenu Quebec or the Registraire where a virtual office and non-resident UBO/management structure are combined; higher for QST registration and commercial-substance verification in the post-production and AI-services sector.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c. S-31.1, arts. 16, 17, 28-30 (incorporation by articles); art. 50 (registered office); arts. 68-69 (officers); Failure to file annual declaration triggers dissolution under art. 126.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Deputy Registrar of Enterprises, online portal CLIC (clic.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts de constitution) submitted electronically; accompanied by the enterprise registration declaration (déclaration d'immatriculation). Total official fee ≈ CAD 520 (CAD 200 deposit + CAD 320 registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Quebec Business Corporations Act; a corporation may be formed with zero paid-up capital. Shares may be subscribed for nominal consideration (e.g., CAD 1.00 per share) fixed by directors; no escrow or trust account is mandated. Non-cash consideration must be valued per art. 34 QBCA. Non-resident ownership is permitted without restriction.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation confirms its lawful incorporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c. S-31.1) and approves the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED, that the subscription for the authorized common shares be and the same is hereby accepted, and share certificates be issued accordingly to the initial subscribers. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at 1000 de la Gauchetière Street, Montreal, Quebec, H3B 4W5, and the corporate minute book be maintained there. RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until their successors are duly elected. RESOLVED, that the Corporation open banking accounts with a Schedule I bank and authorize any two officers jointly to sign cheques and execute all corporate filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Service de réservation de noms / Government of Canada NUANS database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request through a REQ-accredited agent, an online NUANS vendor, or directly at the REQ counter. Select a name with three components: distinctive element (e.g., 'NeuroSub'), descriptive element ('AI Post-Production'), and legal element ('Inc.'). Verify the name is not confusingly similar to an existing trademark or corporation and that it complies with the Charter of the French Language (French required for the distinctive name unless a bilingual or verified English name exemption applies). Reserve the name for a 90-day period.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS name search request form
Proposed corporate name and corporate legal element
Proof of identity of the incorporator (passport or driver's licence)
Authorizing resolution or power of attorney if filing via agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ refuses the name for confusion or prohibited-language reasons, obtain a fresh NUANS report with a modified distinctive element and re-submit. If the name is refused, file an appeal with the Registraire under art. 17 QBCA; alternatively, incorporate using the legal number as the name (e.g., '3218405 Canada Inc.') without further clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator (sole or joint subscribers); notarization not required for electronic filing; legal counsel may prepare draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles in the online CLIC portal or in a formatted PDF in accordance with the QBCA and the forms prescribed by the Registraire. Specify: corporate name; registered office address located in Quebec; authorized share structure (e.g., unlimited Class A common shares, Class B preferred shares with amending restrictions); maximum number and categories of directors (minimum one natural person); any restrictions on share transfers; and any authorization for the Board to implement share subscription agreements. Execute the Articles by the incorporator(s) with full legal names. For online filing, use the secure electronic signature issued by the REQ (clic).
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (arts. 16-17 QBCA)
NUANS name reservation certificate
List of proposed directors and their consents
Registered office address in Quebec (actual street address, not a post office box)
Incorporator's declaration of eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of irregularities or deficiency, correct the specified fields and re-submit the Articles within 30 days of the notice. If the filing is rejected, re-file with a new payment of fees; no appeal exists for purely typographical errors, but the REQ will accept a written explanation and corrected filing without penalty if the issue was administrative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles and Enterprise Registration with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Registraire's CLIC online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ CLIC portal, select 'Dépôt de statuts de constitution', upload the executed Articles, and simultaneously submit the enterprise registration declaration (déclaration d'immatriculation). The system calculates the deposit fee (CAD 200) and registration fee (CAD 320) for a legal person; pay by pre-authorized debit, Visa/Mastercard, or Interac Online. Upon successful processing, the REQ issues the Certificate of Constitution (certificat de constitution) and the enterprise registration certificate, together with the nine-digit Québec enterprise number (NEQ). The statutory publication process (in the Gazette officielle du Québec) is handled administratively by REQ.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation in accepted format
NUANS name reservation certificate
Payment authorization for CAD 520 total fee
Enterprise registration declaration with officer and principal activity fields (NAICS 512191)
Consent to act from each initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ returns a query (demande de renseignements) under art. 30 QBCA, respond in writing within the prescribed deadline (typically 15 days) with the requested clarifications; attachment of a supplementary resolution or corrected share schedule usually cures the defect. If the constitutional deadline (90 days from the date of the first draft) expires, the application is deemed abandoned and a new filing with new fees is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Certification Organizational Acts: Registered Office, Minute Book, and By-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Constitution, hold the first organizational meeting or adopt written resolutions in lieu of a meeting (permitted under art. 122 QBCA). Adopt model by-laws governing share issuance, director meetings, quorum, and signing authority; formally confirm the registered office address in Quebec; and open a corporate minute book with Articles, Certificate, by-laws, directors' register, and securities register. Issue the authorized common shares to subscribers and record share subscription agreements. Ensure the registered office is physically in Quebec and that all registers are available for inspection.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Constitution issued by REQ
Enterprise registration certificate (NEQ)
Draft by-laws (art. 105 QBCA)
Minute book with share certificates and registers
Consents of officers and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board fails to adopt by-laws or issue shares within a reasonable period, the Registrar may apply for court supervision; as a remedy, shareholders holding at least 10% of voting shares may apply to the Superior Court of Quebec for an order directing the board to conduct the organizational acts. Failure to maintain a registered office address can lead to revocation of the enterprise registration; submit an immediate declaration of change to REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec (Registre des contribuables)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register online with the CRA for the federal Business Number (BN) and the following program accounts: corporate income tax (RC0001), GST/HST (RT0001) for annual sales above CAD 30,000, and payroll deductions (RP0001) if the corporation will remunerate directors or employees. Separately register with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST – TVQ) account and the province's source deductions account (known as 'DAS' – deductions at source). Provide the NEQ, registered office address, and the director's SIN. Note that the ministerial mandate (Revenu Québec) issues the 'certificat d'inscription au fichier de la TVQ' upon confirmation of the QST account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Constitution and NEQ
Registered office address proof (lease or utility bill)
Director identification (passport, driver's licence)
Bank account details (for GST/QST refunds)
Copy of first board resolution confirming tax compliance responsibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account application is queried, respond to CRA/Revenu Québec within 30 days with the requested supporting documents. Late registrations attract penalties for failure to register; however, the CRA's Voluntary Disclosures Program (VDP) and Revenu Québec's equivalent 'divulgation volontaire' program allow the corporation to apply for relief from penalties and partial interest when disclosure is made before enforcement action has started.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal and Sectoral Registration, and Opening of Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal administration (e.g., Ville de Montréal – Permis d'exploitation); Schedule I Bank (e.g., RBC, BMO, TD, Desjardins)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the municipal authorities for any business scope permit required by the local zoning by-law. For a post-production studio operating in an office/commercial zone, a 'permis d'exploitation' or 'certificat d'occupation' may be required; confirm that the premises zoning permits audiovisual post-production use (NAICS 512191). Open a corporate bank account with a Schedule I bank or credit union (e.g., Desjardins) presenting the certificate of constitution, NEQ, by-laws, and board resolution; provide beneficial ownership declaration to comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Deposit the initial share subscription proceeds and issue the final share certificates.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Constitution and NEQ
First board resolution on banking and authorized signatories
Municipal business permit application (zoning and occupancy)
Beneficial ownership declaration forms for KYC
Lease agreement for the registered premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is refused by reason of zoning, apply for a 'dérogation mineure' (minor variance) before the city's Committee on Zoning, or lease alternative premises. If the bank refuses the account for incomplete KYC, furnish the missing beneficial ownership statements and re-apply; financial institutions may require the seal or a legal opinion confirming corporate existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Declaration and Statutory Compliance Calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately upon incorporation, note the mandatory annual declaration of the enterprise with REQ (due within 60 days after each anniversary date, but no later than the third anniversary for renewal), and the annual corporate income tax return (federal T2 and Quebec CO-17). Implement a compliance calendar for: filing GST/HST and QST returns (monthly/quarterly/yearly depending on revenues); remitting payroll source deductions (CRA and Revenu Québec); holding annual shareholder meetings within 15 months pursuant to art. 102 QBCA; and filing director disclosures. Ensure that the minute book and registers are updated with each director change.
required_dossiers: REQ annual declaration confirmation (electronic form)
Federal T2 return and schedules
Quebec CO-17 return and remittance confirmation
Payroll remittance summaries (CRA RP, Revenu Québec DAS)
Minutes of annual shareholder and board meetings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ initiates dissolution for failure to file annual declarations, the corporation may apply for reinstatement within 3 years by filing all omitted declarations and paying the penalty (CAD 50 per declaration). For missed tax filings, use the CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program and Revenu Québec voluntary disclosure before any demand letter is sent; pay all arrears and interest to limit penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) du Québec — no industrial licence is applicable to a sound/subtitle post-production studio; any municipal 'permis d'exploitation' is delivered by the local administration (e.g., Ville de Montréal – Direction des permis commerciaux).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the AI subtitle transcription and voice cloning activity (NAICS 512191) is a service-based professional activity outside the regulated occupations; no provincial operating licence, telecommunications licence, or broadcasting certificate is required where there is no over-the-air transmission or distribution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the post-production studio activity does not appear in Schedule 1 of the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 23, REAFIE); consequently, no full EIA study or MELCCFP attestation is required. A municipal certificate of occupancy verifying the premises comply with the Quebec Construction Code and fire safety rules will cover physical installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge limited to domestic-scale sanitary flows to the municipal sanitary sewer per municipal sewer by-law (e.g., Montreal by-law CA-15) and the Regulation respecting municipal wastewater treatment works; no industrial process wastewater. Emissions: no VOC or hazardous air emissions expected from AI computing and recording equipment; ozone-depleting substances from HVAC equipment handled per the Environment Quality Act and the federal Ozone-depleting Substances Regulations; electronic waste (servers, GPU units, media) managed under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 40.1) with an approved recovery service; waste solvents and lithium batteries segregated and shipped by a permitted transporter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain a fire safety certificate from the competent municipal fire prevention service (e.g., Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal) verifying compliance with the Quebec Fire Safety Code (IFC); maintain portable extinguishers, exit signage, and emergency lighting. Structural: occupancy permit issued under the Quebec Building Code (RBQ) confirming the floors' static load capacity for heavy acoustic isolation and equipment racks; electrical installation certificate issued by a master electrician under the Quebec Electrical Code. Labour: register with the CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) for occupational health and safety, submit a hazard identification and prevention program, and implement a workplace hazardous materials information system (WHMIS) for cleaning agents.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal Income Tax Act and GST/HST; portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes.html). Quebec: Revenu Québec — QST and provincial corporate tax; portal: Mon dossier d'entreprise (https://www.revenuquebec.ca). Export customs: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) (https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Incorporate the Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act (federal) or the Quebec Business Corporations Act; for Quebec operations obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ). STEP 2: Apply to CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number); non-resident corporations may file RC1 by mail or fax with applicable schedules and must provide foreign registration/TIN evidence plus a Canadian address for service; no minimum capital is required. STEP 3: Register for GST/HST online through CRA My Business Account or with the RC1; registration is mandatory once taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000; a foreign entity may voluntarily register to recover input tax credits. STEP 4: Register with Revenu Québec for QST using the prescribed registration form (LM-1-V, Registration Form for the GST/HST and QST) or the online service in Mon dossier d'entreprise, and separately register for Quebec payroll and source deductions if employees are engaged in Quebec. STEP 5: Maintain the federal BN and the Quebec NEQ, appoint a tax services representative in Canada if the corporation is non-resident, and file all returns electronically (NETFILE for GST/HST; Revenu Québec electronic transmission for QST).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Corporation is a distinct taxpayer from its shareholders (Income Tax Act s.15); a resident corporation (central management and control in Canada) is taxed on worldwide income (ITA s.2(1)); a non-resident corporation is taxed only on Canadian-source business income, is subject to Part XIII withholding on dividends and interest, and may incur a 25% Part XIV branch profits tax (treaty-reduced). No pass-through treatment is available; Quebec imposes a separate entity-level provincial income tax under the Taxation Act (Québec).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in Canada. Elections available include: (i) ITA s.85(1) rollover election on transfer of property to the corporation to defer capital gains; (ii) association-status election under ITA s.256(2.1) for Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) planning; (iii) ITA s.216 net-basis election for non-residents earning Canadian rental or timber royalties (treaty-enabled); (iv) Excise Tax Act s.156 election for supplies between closely-related corporations to neutralize GST/HST; (v) the corresponding QST election for closely-related corporations under the Quebec Sales Tax Act; and (vi) hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss.18.4-18.6) and the Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses Limitation (EIFEL, ITA ss.18.2-18.3), which are mandatory anti-avoidance provisions accompanied by tax-credit timing elections under ITA s.20(11)-(12). None of these elections converts a Business Corporation into a pass-through entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — federal value-added tax (Excise Tax Act Part IX); QST — Quebec Sales Tax (Quebec Sales Tax Act); integrated consumption tax with input tax credit mechanism; exports of goods and most services to non-residents are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. Small-supplier threshold for GST/HST (ETA s.148(1)) and QST (QSA s.16), measured over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters of worldwide taxable supplies; a non-resident supplier of digital services (including AI subtitling and voice-cloning products) must register once the CAD 30,000 threshold is met; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold to recover input tax credits; separate QST registration is mandatory when a commercial activity is carried on in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping exists in Canada. The CRA operates a voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing pilot using the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 standard; B2G invoices must be submitted through federal supplier portals. Registered businesses must file GST/HST returns electronically via NETFILE and QST returns through Revenu Québec electronic transmission; electronic books and records must be retained in a machine-readable format and produced to CRA or Revenu Québec within prescribed timelines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported qualify for zero-rating under ETA Schedule VI Part V ss.1-6. Services supplied to a non-resident, including AI subtitle transcription and AI voice-cloning studio services, are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI Part V s.7 (supplies to non-residents) where the service is not performed in respect of Canadian real property or tangible personal property and is not received in Canada by the non-resident; the QST mirror rule applies under the Quebec Sales Tax Regulations Schedule VI Part V s.7. A contract with a Canadian resident studio client does not qualify; the payer's location, place of performance, contract governing law, and digital delivery logs determine eligibility. B2B services received in Canada are subject to 5% GST plus 9.975% QST (14.975% combined).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: B13A Canada Export Declaration / Customs Coding Form (required only for physical media or goods; service exports are evidenced by a service export worksheet and delivery logs)
Duly executed service agreement with the non-resident client (governing law, place of performance, delivery terms, foreign TIN of the client)
Commercial invoice referencing the zero-rated export and the ETA Schedule VI citation
Bill of lading, airway bill, or electronic export manifest (for goods) plus digital delivery access logs and IP trails (for services)
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank statement evidencing cross-border FX proceeds from the non-resident buyer
Non-resident status evidence: foreign tax registration number, certificate of residence, and declaration that the service is not consumed in Canada
GST/HST and QST returns with the zero-rated export schedules and the related input tax credit calculation
GST189 (General Application for GST/HST Rebate) where a rebate is claimed, plus transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany export transactions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within a 4-year limitation period; the period is unlimited in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful default (ITA s.152(4); QTA s.1016; ETA s.298). False or inflated export zero-rating claims attract gross negligence penalties of 50% of the understated tax (ITA s.163(2); ETA s.285.1) plus specified false-statement penalties; criminal evasion under ETA s.327 or ITA s.239 carries fines up to CAD 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Reassessed export zero-ratings claw back input tax credits and rebates with compounded daily arrears interest at the CRA prescribed rate (currently approximately 5%-9% per annum). Export refund applications are barred unless filed within the two-year window (ETA s.296(2.1) and QST equivalent). Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/HST and QST (ITA s.227.1; ETA s.323; QSA parallel), and fraudulent FX or export documentation triggers parallel AML review and transfer-pricing penalties under ITA s.247.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully convertible currency regime for both capital and current account transactions. Residents and non-residents may freely convert CAD to foreign currencies and vice versa without prior regulatory approval. Profit remittances by Canadian corporations are unrestricted provided they comply with corporate tax filing obligations, beneficial ownership disclosure requirements, and anti-money laundering standards.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists for mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts or converted to CAD at the exporter's sole discretion. All transactions remain subject to anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing reporting thresholds and must be supported by verifiable trade documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for offshore digital EMIs through regulated platforms such as Wise and Stripe. Legal constraints are limited to mandatory compliance with Canadian AML/KYC obligations, beneficial ownership verification, and transaction reporting; no outright prohibition exists for legitimate cross-border payment services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding with video KYC is permitted for standard corporate accounts at Tier 1 banks. Physical presence of directors is not mandatory for routine incorporation and account opening; however, enhanced due diligence requiring in-person interviews may be triggered for accounts exceeding prescribed transaction thresholds or involving higher-risk counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds or links to high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate charter and articles of incorporation, beneficial ownership declaration with supporting identification, audited financial statements, bank reference letters, trade contracts, and proof of legitimate business operations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers using purpose code 848 (Capital Contribution) or 880 (Equity Injection). Verification requires corporate resolution authorizing the injection, share issuance documentation, beneficial ownership certificates, and source-of-funds evidence. All wires must include the recipient bank's full details and purpose code for regulatory compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or issuance of commercial letters of credit through correspondent banking networks. Trade settlements require supporting documentation including signed contracts, invoices, packing lists, and proof of delivery. Commercial LCs are processed under UCP 600 rules with clear beneficiary and applicant details.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD $12 late-filing penalty plus interest; administrative dissolution after two consecutive missed filings (QBCA s.259).
Greater of $100 or 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on balances.
5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month (max 12); statutory interest under the Tax Administration Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; subject to REQ inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual declaration date; within 15 days of any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors' liability; penal fine up to CAD $5,000 for non-maintenance or false registration (QBCA s.125.2).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Register Audit and Board Minute Certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prior to the annual declaration deadline; at each fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inadequate books/registers may preclude comfort letters and subject directors to personal liability under QBCA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a private, non-distributing Quebec corporation if all shareholders consent in writing to waive auditor appointment (QBCA s.206); public/listing entities and any corporation triggering shareholder requisition remain audit-mandatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private Canadian entities use ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II); public entities use IFRS. Corporate tax filings follow Canadian GAAP with tax reconciliations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under QBCA s.125.1, the company must maintain a register of beneficial owners; each person with control/significant influence must annually confirm or update their information in writing, and the company must capture changes within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Copies of annual declarations filed with REQ

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate income tax rate for Quebec corporations: 15% federal plus 11.5% Quebec. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally access a combined small-business rate of approximately 12.2% on eligible active business income within the applicable small-business limits, subject to federal and Quebec rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential incentives include the federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development program, Quebec research and development tax credits, Quebec multimedia and cultural production credits where statutory conditions are met, the federal and Quebec manufacturing and processing regimes where applicable, and the federal general tax reduction. The SR&ED rate depends on corporation type, taxable capital, ownership, expenditure eligibility, and expenditure limits. Film, digital-media, and cultural credits require separate sector-specific eligibility and certification; an automated subtitle, dubbing, or AI voice-cloning business is not automatically eligible.
corporate_income_tax_regime.actual_loss_rules_note: The supplied schema requires a value of 5, but Canadian law does not generally impose a five-year corporate loss carryforward limit. Federal and Quebec non-capital losses are generally carryforward for 20 taxation years and back three taxation years, subject to continuity and acquisition-of-control rules. Net capital losses are generally carried forward indefinitely and back three taxation years against taxable capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through CRA-certified tax software or an authorized electronic filing channel. Related schedules commonly include Schedule 1, Schedule 8, Schedule 9, Schedule 23 where applicable, Schedule 50, Schedule 100, Schedule 125, Schedule 141, Schedule 150, Schedule 200, and Form T106 for reportable non-arm's-length non-resident transactions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporate income tax installments are generally required monthly or quarterly during the taxation year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return is due within six months after the end of every taxation year. Any balance is generally due two months after year-end; an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation may qualify for a three-month balance-due period if the statutory conditions are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, corporation type, address, taxation-year start and end dates, incorporation details, province of residence, and fiscal-period information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada must identify its Canadian permanent establishment or business activities, report Canadian-source business income, and maintain records supporting the allocation of income and expenses to Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation ownership, associated corporations, control, and Canadian-controlled private corporation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign ownership, non-resident control, associated entities, and any circumstances affecting CCPC status. A corporation controlled directly or indirectly by non-residents generally cannot claim CCPC treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income or loss to income for tax purposes, including non-deductible expenses, reserves, depreciation, provisions, and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude non-Canadian income unless required under the applicable Canadian residence or source rules, but include Canadian permanent-establishment income and make transfer-pricing and branch-allocation adjustments where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance, eligible property classes, additions, disposals, recapture, terminal losses, and immediate-expensing or accelerated-investment claims where available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only Canadian tax depreciation permitted for property used to earn Canadian business income and retain acquisition, use, ownership, and disposition documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder information for specified shareholders and other ownership-related disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report material non-resident shareholders and ownership information accurately. Ownership disclosure should reconcile with corporate registers, beneficial ownership records, and Schedule 9.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement information and accounting-policy, ownership, and tax-preparer information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use financial statements prepared on a consistent basis and reconcile Canadian branch or subsidiary accounts to the consolidated group accounts without concealing related-party transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax calculation, refundable and non-refundable credits, tax payable, installments, and balance owing or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute federal tax only on the corporation's taxable Canadian income and claim foreign tax credits, treaty positions, and tax credits only when supported by statutory records and applicable limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 or applicable small-business schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Small-business deduction and associated-corporation allocation, where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled corporation normally does not qualify as a CCPC and should not claim the small-business deduction without confirming every statutory condition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents of Canada.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File for reportable transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents when the aggregate reportable transaction amount exceeds CAD 1 million, subject to statutory exclusions and filing rules. Reconcile amounts to intercompany agreements, invoices, and transfer-pricing records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late-filing penalty is generally 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% of unpaid tax for each full month late, up to 12 months; higher repeated-failure penalties may apply. Interest is compounded daily at the prescribed rate. Additional penalties may apply for false statements, omissions, failure to file T106, failure to provide information, or late elections. Directors may become personally liable for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST in specified circumstances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through Revenu Quebec's approved transmission system or certified tax software. Related filings may include CO-771, CO-1029.8.36.5, CO-1029.8.33.6, CO-1029.8.36.7, and other credit, loss, installment, and ownership schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; Quebec corporate tax installments are generally required monthly or quarterly depending on statutory eligibility.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The CO-17 return is generally due within six months after the end of the corporation's taxation year. Quebec tax balances are generally payable two months after year-end, subject to applicable small-corporation rules and exceptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number, federal business number, legal name, address, taxation year, corporation type, and Quebec filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation carrying on business in Quebec must register and report Quebec taxable income based on its Quebec allocation, permanent establishment, payroll, gross revenue, and applicable allocation factors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting income reconciliation, Quebec-specific additions and deductions, capital cost allowance, reserves, losses, and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a defensible Quebec allocation of revenue, payroll, expenses, intellectual-property functions, and personnel activity. Do not allocate income to Quebec solely through contractual labels.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income, applicable rates, credits, installments, tax payable, and refund or balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Quebec general rate or qualifying reduced rates only where statutory conditions are met. Reconcile the Quebec return with the federal T2 and explain material differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development, multimedia, cultural, employment, investment, and other Quebec tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by Quebec certifications, eligible expenditure records, project descriptions, payroll records, and contemporaneous technical documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Employer source deductions, RL-1 slips, non-resident withholding, and related information reporting where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Register as an employer where Quebec employees or deemed employees are present, withhold required amounts, and distinguish employee compensation from contractor payments using factual status tests.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec late-filing penalties, interest, and administrative penalties may apply to unpaid tax, late returns, inaccurate information, failure to remit source deductions, and failure to provide records. Interest is generally compounded according to prescribed rates. Exact Quebec penalties depend on the violation, duration, amount, repetition, and whether a demand or assessment has been issued.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid or credited by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident, subject to treaty reduction, statutory exemptions, and anti-avoidance rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payer should obtain a valid Form NR301, NR302, or NR303, as applicable, or equivalent documentary evidence establishing the recipient's residence, beneficial ownership, and treaty entitlement before applying a reduced rate. A certificate of residence or tax residency certificate should be obtained where required by the treaty or CRA administrative practice. The payer must apply reasonable-care procedures, retain support, remit withholding to the CRA by the 15th day of the month following payment, file the applicable NR4 information return and slips, and report the treaty article and reduced rate. Treaty relief is not automatic where the recipient is an agent, conduit, fiscally transparent entity, nominee, or person lacking beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Part XIII rates are generally 25% for royalties and other amounts paid to non-residents; most arm's-length interest paid by a Canadian resident to a non-resident is exempt from Part XIII withholding, subject to statutory exceptions. Under the Canada-China income tax treaty, dividends are generally limited to 10% where the beneficial owner is a company meeting the required voting-interest threshold and 15% otherwise; interest is generally limited to 10%; royalties are generally limited to 10%, subject to treaty definitions and special categories. The applicable treaty must be verified for the recipient's residence and payment type. Software, voice models, datasets, cloud services, technical services, and licensing arrangements must be classified based on legal rights and facts rather than invoice labels.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For Canadian cross-border non-arm's-length transactions, contemporaneous documentation is required under section 247 of the Income Tax Act. Form T106 reporting is generally triggered when aggregate reportable non-arm's-length non-resident transactions exceed CAD 1 million, subject to exclusions. Canada does not impose a universal OECD-style separate Local File or Master File filing threshold; section 247 documentation must nevertheless support the arm's-length result, and the CRA may require organized transaction-level and group-level information.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other method producing the most reliable arm's-length result where the listed methods are not appropriate
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no general standalone Economic Substance Regulation equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance remains material under section 247 transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, treaty principal-purpose and limitation provisions where applicable, beneficial-ownership analysis, corporate-residence rules, foreign-affiliate rules, and interest-deductibility rules. The corporation should maintain Canadian personnel, decision-making, functions, assets, risks, contracts, payroll, premises, and operational records consistent with the profits allocated to Quebec and Canada. AI voice-cloning and subtitle operations require documented ownership, development, licensing, data-governance, cybersecurity, and intellectual-property functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating revenue, fabricating expenses, concealing payment-rail receipts, claiming unsupported SR&ED or cultural credits, or submitting materially false T2 or CO-17 information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the federal Income Tax Act, conviction for tax evasion may result in a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment of up to five years. Civil reassessment, gross-negligence penalties, interest, and provincial penalties may apply. Fraudulent or forged records may also engage the Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face criminal prosecution where personal participation or authorization is proven. Personal liability is not automatic for ordinary corporate income tax, but directors may be liable for unremitted source deductions, GST/HST, and certain deemed-trust amounts after statutory conditions are satisfied. Imprisonment is possible for conviction; travel restrictions are not automatic but may arise from bail, court orders, or enforcement proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File, Remit, or Maintain Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Late or missing T2 or CO-17 returns, failure to remit installments or withholding, failure to issue NR4 or RL slips, or destruction or non-production of books and records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalties, failure-to-file penalties, prescribed interest, director-assessment exposure for source deductions and GST/HST, and penalties for failure to provide information may apply. Repeated non-compliance can lead to enforced collection, garnishment, liens, and prosecution in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed personally for certain unremitted trust amounts if they failed to exercise the statutory due diligence defence. Corporate debts generally remain corporate debts, but personal guarantees, fraudulent conduct, oppression, and statutory director-liability provisions can create direct exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, AI-development fees, financing costs, or data-license fees without commercial support; allocating residual profit to a low-substance foreign entity; or omitting T106 reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may adjust taxable income under section 247, impose transfer-pricing penalties generally equal to 10% of the applicable adjustment in qualifying circumstances, deny deductions, apply withholding tax, and charge interest. Reassessments may extend beyond ordinary periods in cases of misrepresentation or neglect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure for knowingly participating in fraud, false records, or tax evasion. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments do not automatically pierce the corporate veil or create personal income-tax liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, royalties, or interest through an intermediary that is not the beneficial owner, misrepresenting residence, using an invalid tax residency certificate, or applying treaty relief without reasonable-care documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unwithheld Part XIII tax, interest, and penalties. Treaty benefits may be denied under beneficial-ownership principles, anti-conduit principles, the principal-purpose test where applicable, or the general anti-avoidance rule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers may face civil or criminal exposure for knowing false certifications or deliberate withholding failures. A corporate veil is not ordinarily pierced solely because treaty relief was incorrectly applied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Sham Arrangement, or Artificial Residence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal Canadian corporation with no genuine business, employees, management, assets, or risk assumption while booking Canadian or treaty-favored income solely to obtain tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may deny deductions, credits, treaty benefits, or Canadian residence claims; recharacterize transactions under the general anti-avoidance rule; assess withholding and penalties; and impose interest. Sham transactions and fraudulent documentation may result in criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling persons may be personally liable for fraudulent conduct, statutory trust amounts, or criminal offences. Imprisonment may apply after conviction; travel bans are not an automatic corporate-tax sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Stripe, Wise, banking channels, or crypto-related intermediaries to conceal beneficial owners, launder proceeds, evade sanctions, falsify customer identity, or fragment transactions to avoid reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties, transaction restrictions, compliance orders, and criminal prosecution may apply. Criminal laundering or proceeds-of-crime offences can result in substantial fines and imprisonment, including imprisonment of up to ten years or more depending on the offence. Sanctions breaches may attract penalties under Canadian sanctions legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and beneficial owners may be prosecuted for knowing participation, authorization, or wilful blindness. Personal asset restraint, forfeiture, prosecution, and court-imposed travel restrictions may occur; none is automatic merely because a corporation received a compliance notice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AI Intellectual-Property, Privacy, and Data-Governance Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using voices, scripts, recordings, datasets, or customer content without required consent or license; cloning a person's voice deceptively; transferring personal data without appropriate safeguards; or misrepresenting AI-generated content.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil injunctions, damages, accounting of profits, statutory copyright remedies where available, privacy complaints, regulatory orders, contractual claims, and reputational loss may arise. Criminal exposure depends on facts such as fraud, identity offences, unauthorized access, or deliberate misappropriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure for intentional torts, knowing authorization, fraud, or statutory offences. Corporate status does not shield a person who personally commits or directs the unlawful act.
